'''David Gamarnik''' is an American [[applied mathematician]], and a Nanyang Technological University Professor in the Operations Research and Statistics Group at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]'s [[Sloan School of Management]].<ref name="mit-sloan">{{Cite web |title=David D. Gamarnik |url=https://mitsloan.mit.edu/faculty/directory/david-d-gamarnik |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> His research spans discrete probability, statistics and machine learning, algorithms and optimization, quantum computing, stochastic processes and queueing theory.<ref name="cv">{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae – David Gamarnik |url=https://www.mit.edu/~gamarnik/CV.pdf |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Gamarnik was born in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] and completed part of his undergraduate studies at [[Tbilisi State University]] in 1990. He received a B.A. in mathematics from [[New York University]], [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] in 1993.<ref name="cv" /> He received his Ph.D. in Operations Research from [[MIT]] in 1998, with a dissertation titled ''Stability and Performance of Multiclass Queueing Networks''.<ref name="dspace">{{Cite web |title=Stability and performance of multiclass queueing networks |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/10064 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gamarnik worked as a research staff member at [[IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center]] (1997–2005).<ref name="cv" /> He joined the [[MIT]] [[Sloan School of Management]] in 2005, serving as an Assistant Professor (2005–2007), Associate Professor (2007–2012), and full Professor (since 2012).<ref name="cv" />

He has written over 150 scientific publications and a textbook, and made profound contributions to numerous domains, including discrete probability, random structures, algorithms and combinatorial optimization, statistics and machine learning, quantum computing, stochastic processes, as well as queueing theory.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=David Gamarnik named IMS Fellow
 |url=https://stat.mit.edu/news/david-gamarnik-named-ims-fellow/
 |website=MIT Statistics and Data Science Center
 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology
 |date=2023-05-15
 |access-date=2026-03-13
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Plenary Speakers |website=INFORMS Applied Probability Society Conference |url=https://informs-aps.isye.gatech.edu/speakers/plenary-speakers |access-date=2026-03-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2011 Best Publication Award citation |website=The Applied Probability Society of INFORMS |url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/INFORMS/50069173-2ea8-479b-baa7-2071ed7cd5dc/UploadedImages/Bestpub_2011_citation.pdf |format=PDF |access-date=2026-03-13}}</ref>

Along with [[Madhu Sudan]], he introduced Overlap Gap Property, a new method for understanding [[average-case complexity]], based on theory of [[spin glasses]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Tackling hard computational problems

 |author=Michael J. Sweet
 |date=2022-10-13
 |access-date=2026-03-13
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |title=A Breakthrough in Global Dynamics on Graphs
 |url=https://www.mathinstitutes.org/highlights/slmath-2025-global-dynamics-on-graphs
 |website=MathInstitutes.org
 |author=Siobhan Roberts
 |date=2025-10-01
 |access-date=2026-03-13
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web

 |website=Facebook
 |access-date=2026-03-13
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Müller |first=Noela |title=Is it easier to find half a needle than a full needle in a random network? |website=The Network Pages |date=2023-05-03 |url=https://www.networkpages.nl/is-it-easier-to-find-half-a-needle-than-a-full-needle-in-a-random-network/ |access-date=2026-03-13}}</ref>

He has served in editorial roles (area editor/associate editor) for premier operations research and applied probability journals, including ''[[Mathematics of Operations Research]]'', the ''[[Annals of Applied Probability]]'', ''[[Queueing Systems]]'', ''[[Stochastic Systems]]'', and [[Operations Research (journal)|''Operations Research'']].<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |website=Mathematics of Operations Research |publisher=INFORMS |url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/page/moor/editorial-board |access-date=2026-03-13}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Gamarnik has received multiple honors and awards from professional societies, including:
* Erlang Prize (Applied Probability Society of [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences|INFORMS]], 2004)<ref name="ormstoday2004">{{Cite web |title=INFORMS Subdivision Awards (Erlang Prize, 2004) |url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/do/10.1287/orms.2005.02.23in/full/ |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>
* INFORMS Applied Probability Society Best Publication Award (2011)<ref name="informs-awards">{{Cite web |title=David Gamarnik – Award Recipient |url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Award-Recipients/David-Gamarnik |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>
* INFORMS Franz Edelman Prize Laureate (2014)<ref name="edelman2014">{{Cite web |title=Franz Edelman Laureates: Class of 2014 |url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/INFORMS-Prizes/Franz-Edelman-Award/Franz-Edelman-Laureates2/Franz-Edelman-Laureates-Class-of-2014 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>
* Fellow of INFORMS (2021)<ref name="informsfellows2021">{{Cite web |title=INFORMS Fellows: Class of 2021 |url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Fellows/INFORMS-Fellows-Class-of-2021 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (Class of 2022)<ref name="amsfellows2022">{{Cite web |title=2022 Class of Fellows of the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2022 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (2023)<ref name="imsfellows2023">{{Cite web |title=2023 IMS Fellows Announced |url=https://imstat.org/2023/05/02/2023-ims-fellows-announced/ |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>
